question: Can elementary action programs discover a mixing reversible braid and its undo and use one frozen communication policy to follow new read wiring?
inputs: Six raw Boolean wires for a pair of ternary values; finite structural reward. For transfer, a crossed nine-bit relation, two frames, and nine public delayed-read ports with literal coordinate pins.
forbidden_inputs: No crossing/undo primitive, named example table, compiler from a supplied transformation, copied inverse program, labels of optimal widths or compatible ports, refitting on test wiring, actual query during encoding, or lingering source access at the receiver.
mapping: Induce two independent collections of bounded Boolean expressions, then fit shared per-cell read and slot-reuse transitions by terminal reward. Freeze one joint checkpoint before scoring held-out behavior.
primary_observable: Actual forward and inverse, held-out braid and long-word results, chosen payload widths against the number of possible downstream answer vectors, physical packet collisions, joint relation reconstruction, and same-world rewiring.
comparators_or_controls: Zero-gate identity and swap, withheld braid reward, stale or one-slot reads, marginally indistinguishable relation pairs, and the three cells plus their redundant union.
resource_budget: Bounded finite Boolean semantic catalogue and one deterministic fit. The relation census uses 512 tables; one single-core shared-runner unit, with an independent raw-checkpoint verifier.
first_executable_signal: Recovered gate programs mix and undo all nine points; under one unaltered checkpoint a rewiring can change a one-bit exact read to a nine-bit joint read.
stop_rule: Preserve partial results, shortcuts and over-wide encodings. The deployed learner and all comparison roles are declared before the run.
